query: facility managers don't notice new alerts; make exceptions the first thing they see on the dashboard without redesigning it

mode_evidence: audit: problem statement on existing UI

required.reason: audit mode: operability is part of the review
numbers, tables or charts are the content

recommended.reason: audits check that actions are discoverable and confirmed

required_concepts.reason: asynchronous or remote data on this screen
web content must be keyboard operable
web is used with touch as well as pointer

core.title: Analytical console
core.guidance: Charts are the imagery; one chart palette; modules sized by importance not by a uniform card grid; dark-first tonal surfaces with the accent reserved for alerts and selection; large readable numerics; small multiples over spaghetti charts. Distinctiveness via chart mark style and a signature numeric typeface.
core.use_when: Monitoring and analysis: dashboards with real questions, alerting, drill-down, often on dark themes for long sessions or wall displays.

core.title: KPI / stat tile
core.guidance: Label, value with unit and tabular figures, comparison (vs previous period) with sign + arrow + colour, optional sparkline, consistent decimal precision, the most important KPI larger or first, no icon per tile unless it disambiguates, whole tile links to the detail. Avoid the 'four identical cards with big numbers and a gradient' default.
core.avoid_when: More than ~6 KPIs in a row (users stop reading); KPIs without context (no comparison, no unit).

core.title: Chart container and interaction
covers: chart form chosen from the analytical question
accessible chart summary and table alternative
core.guidance: Title that states the question, unit and time range visible, legend as direct labels where possible, tooltip also keyboard-reachable (focusable points or a data table toggle), accessible summary text, consistent palette, responsive (reduce ticks, not data), empty/loading/error states, no animation beyond a single load transition and none on data refresh. Provide the data table or CSV.
core.avoid_when: Decorative charts with no question; charts of fewer than ~4 points (use a stat).

implementation.react: Recharts/Visx/ECharts already in the project; add role=img + aria-label summary and a table fallback.

core.selected_for: required coverage: accessibility, no colour alone for status, accessible chart summary and table alternative, chart form chosen from the analytical question, loading, empty and error states

core.title: Real-time streams → rolling window charts
core.guidance: Fixed time window that scrolls, stable y-range with occasional stepwise rescale, no per-point animation, thresholds drawn as lines with labels, alert states via colour + icon + text, pause on hover/focus, render on canvas/WebGL beyond a few thousand points, and a 'last updated' timestamp. Wall/TV displays: larger type, fewer panels, high contrast.
core.use_when: Monitoring dashboards, telemetry, trading, wall displays.
core.avoid_when: Never animate every tick with transitions; never let the axis rescale continuously (readers lose reference).
core.selected_for: required coverage: exceptions and anomalies first, real-time rolling window and thresholds, last-updated / refresh state

guardrails.title: Everything operable by keyboard, no traps
guardrails.guidance: Tab reaches every control in visual order; composite widgets use arrow keys with a roving tabindex so Tab is not consumed by every cell; Escape closes layers and returns focus to the invoker; nothing traps focus except a modal, and the modal itself must be escapable. Provide a keyboard alternative for every drag interaction.
guardrails.use_when: Every interactive element, including custom widgets, drag/drop, sliders, menus, date pickers, and anything that appears on hover.
guardrails.selected_for: required coverage: interaction, no hover dependence, keyboard navigation and focus order

guardrails.title: Focus visible and not obscured
guardrails.guidance: Focus indicator ≥2 px with ≥3:1 contrast against adjacent colours and against the unfocused state; sticky UI gets scroll-padding so a focused control scrolls into clear view. On TV the indicator must be obvious at 3 m (scale + border/glow).
guardrails.use_when: Every focusable element in every theme; sticky headers, footers, toasts, and cookie banners must never cover the focused element.
guardrails.avoid_when: Never remove focus styles; use :focus-visible to hide them for mouse clicks only.
